question: What primary effect does physical trauma or acute infection have on a patient's metabolic demands?
explanation: Illness and injury put stress on the body, driving up the need for energy and building blocks to repair tissues. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h1)

question: Why is daily nutrition considered as important as recording vital signs in hospital wards?

options.A: Patients cannot be discharged without a full plate
options.B: Food intake directly fuels tissue healing and immune defense
options.C: Dietary charts replace the need for physician rounds
options.D: Hospital accreditation boards mandate food logs over vital signs

explanation: Adequate nutrients provide the biological substrates necessary for recovery and fighting infections, making nutrition a critical clinical parameter. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h1)

question: Within how many hours of hospital admission should nutritional screening ideally take place?
explanation: Early screening allows the care team to spot deficits and start supportive nutrition before severe wasting occurs. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h2)

question: An adult patient lost twelve percent of their body weight over the past four months due to chronic illness. What does this finding indicate?
explanation: Losing over ten percent of body weight in a short span points to severe nutritional compromise that needs immediate intervention. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h2)

question: Which professional should a nurse contact first when a patient exhibits frequent coughing while swallowing food?
explanation: Speech therapists specialize in swallowing disorders and perform assessments to prevent aspiration risks. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h3)

question: Why is the nurse considered the central hub of communication regarding daily inpatient nutrition?

options.A: Dietitians are not allowed to speak directly with patients
options.B: Nurses have the sole authority to prescribe artificial tube feeds
options.C: Physicians delegate all hospital menu planning to nursing staff
options.D: Nurses observe meal consumption and symptoms firsthand at the bedside

explanation: Because nurses spend continuous time with patients, they gather real-time data on appetite and tolerance to share with the wider team. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h3)

question: To what minimum angle should a bed be elevated when assisting an inpatient with oral feeding?
explanation: Sitting upright uses gravity to keep food moving down the esophagus and protects the airway from accidental aspiration. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h4)

question: A nurse is preparing to feed a frail elderly patient in bed. What is the most important preparatory action to take first?

options.A: Order a completely liquid diet from the kitchen
options.B: Turn off all room lights to induce relaxation
options.C: Administer a sleeping pill to calm the patient
options.D: Clear foul odors and clean the patient's hands

explanation: A clean environment and clean hands promote appetite and reduce infection risks during meal consumption. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h4)

question: What is the most precise way for a nurse to document a patient's meal consumption?

options.A: Asking the visitor what the patient liked best
options.B: Writing a vague note stating food was provided
options.C: Estimating the percentage of food eaten from the tray
options.D: Weighing the food tray before it leaves the kitchen

explanation: Recording percentages gives the dietitian and doctor clear data on exact caloric and nutrient intake. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h5)

question: Which clinical sign is most characteristic of early dehydration in a hospitalized adult?

options.A: Lowered resting heart rate and cold skin
options.B: Widespread peripheral edema in the lower legs
options.C: Elevated blood pressure readings throughout the day
options.D: Dry mucous membranes and concentrated urine

explanation: As body water drops, mucous beds lose moisture and the kidneys concentrate urine to conserve fluid. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h5)

question: What is the primary difference between enteral and parenteral nutrition support?

options.A: Enteral uses the GI tract, while parenteral infuses directly into the bloodstream
options.B: Parenteral requires chewing food, while enteral uses pureed liquids
options.C: Parenteral uses feeding tubes, while enteral uses intravenous lines
options.D: Enteral is only used for babies, while parenteral is for adults

explanation: Enteral feeds utilize the gut's natural digestive function, whereas parenteral feeds bypass the digestive system entirely. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h6)

question: Why is strict aseptic technique required when managing total parenteral nutrition lines?

options.A: Central lines are made of fragile materials that dissolve in water
options.B: Skin flora cannot tolerate contact with amino acid solutions
options.C: Parenteral bags contain live microorganisms that must be filtered out
options.D: High sugar solutions promote rapid bacterial growth and systemic infection

explanation: The high concentrations of glucose and amino acids in parenteral solutions make them a fertile breeding ground for bacteria. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h6)

question: What key competency must family members demonstrate before a patient is discharged with a feeding tube?

options.A: Knowledge of hospital billing codes for enteral equipment
options.B: Safe tube flushing, placement checking, and feed administration
options.C: Skill in formulating medical solutions from raw pharmacy chemicals
options.D: Ability to surgically replace the gastrostomy button independently

explanation: Caregivers must prove they can manage the equipment safely at home to prevent blockages or aspiration. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h7)

question: Why must discharge nutritional counseling incorporate culturally appropriate local food options?

options.A: It improves patient adherence when meals match local availability and lifestyle
options.B: Local foods have zero nutritional value compared to imported supplements
options.C: Hospitals lack the budget to print standard diet sheets
options.D: Foreign food items are strictly illegal in community markets

explanation: Patients are far more likely to follow dietary advice when it utilizes affordable, familiar foods found in their community. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h7)

question: Which clinical indicator is commonly tracked to evaluate the success of nutritional therapy over time?
explanation: Consistent weight tracking provides a reliable metric of whether the patient is receiving enough calories. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h8)

question: What should a nurse do when a patient's nutritional care plan fails to stop ongoing weight loss?

options.A: Wait until discharge to mention the weight loss to the doctor
options.B: Assume the patient is lying about what they eat each day
options.C: Update the care plan and request a multidisciplinary team review
options.D: Discontinue all food charts to reduce paperwork in the ward

explanation: Failing interventions require prompt re-evaluation and collaboration with dietitians or physicians to adjust therapy. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h8)
